cover.woman_bio: Born in Tennessee, she had polio as a child and was told she might not walk normally. At the 1960 Rome Olympics she became the first American woman to win three gold medals in one Games (100 m, 200 m and the 4x100 m relay). She refused to attend a segregated victory parade at home, which made it Clarksville’s first integrated event.
cover.quote: Never underestimate the power of dreams and the influence of the human spirit.
cover.quote_source: Wilma Rudolph, widely quoted (Blavity; Sunday Observer)

pomodoros.subject: Writing: one paragraph with a topic sentence and support (essay first)

content.content: Paragraph recipe: (1) topic sentence says the main point; (2) two or three supporting sentences give details or examples; (3) a closing sentence ties back. Every sentence is complete. Join ideas with , and / , but / , so / because.

Model. Practice made me faster. (1) Last month I could not run a mile without stopping. (2) I trained four days a week, so my legs got stronger. (3) Yesterday I ran the whole mile. That is why I believe practice works.

Reading. As a child Wilma Rudolph had polio and wore a leg brace. At the 1960 Rome Olympics she won gold in the 100 m, the 200 m and the 4x100 m relay. Your topic: a time you kept going when others doubted you, or when it was hard.

content.question: Which sentence is the best TOPIC sentence?
choices: B) Wilma Rudolph showed that hard work can beat a hard start.
D) Polio is a disease that, and then.

content.question: Write your topic sentence. Say what the time was and what it showed.
hints: Say what the time was in one sentence: who, what, when.
Frame: “A time I kept going when it was hard was ____.”

content.question: Support 1: a detail or example of what happened.
hints: What happened first? Write one complete sentence with a subject and a verb.

content.question: Support 2: a second detail joined with , and, , but or because.
hints: Add a second detail. Join it with , and / , but / because.

content.question: Closing: start with “That is why” or “This shows”.
hints: Frame: “That is why ____.” Tie back to your topic sentence.

content.question: Fix the fragment: “Because she kept training every day.” Make it a complete sentence.
hints: It needs a main clause. Who did what because of the reason?

content.content: Watch the two videos first. Then: “less than” flips the order (7 less than a number is n − 7). Solve equations by undoing: add/subtract first, then multiply/divide. Always CHECK in the original.

content.question: Which expression means “7 less than 3 times a number n”?
Evaluate 3n − 7 when n = 6.
hints: Replace n with 6, multiply, then subtract 7.

content.question: Solve: 3x + 5 = 20.
hints: Subtract 5 from both sides. Then divide by 3.

content.question: Solve: 4(x − 3) = 20. (Divide by 4 first, or distribute.)
hints: Divide both sides by 4 first. Then add 3.

content.question: Solve: 2x + 7 = 3x − 2. Then CHECK your x in both sides.
hints: Get x on one side: subtract 2x from both sides. Then add 2. Check in both sides.

content.question: Median of 14, 3, 9, 7. (Put in order first; four numbers means average the middle two.)
hints: Order them: 3, 7, 9, 14. Average the two in the middle.

pomodoros.subject: Social Studies: a life, a law, a parade

content.content: Reading. Wilma Rudolph was born in Tennessee in 1940. In 1960 she won three gold medals at the Rome Olympics. When she returned home she refused to attend a victory parade that was segregated, and the parade became Clarksville’s first integrated event.

content.question: How many years after she was born did the Rome Olympics take place?
Segregation means:
choices: A) Keeping groups of people apart by law or custom

content.question: Brown v. Board of Education (1954) ruled that:
choices: C) Segregated public schools were unconstitutional

content.question: Which branch decided Brown?
In 2 complete sentences: why do you think her refusal to attend a segregated parade mattered?

content.content: Passage. Doctors told Wilma Rudolph’s family that she might never walk normally. She wore a brace, and her family helped her with exercises at home. Years later she ran so fast that reporters called her the fastest woman in the world. Her story shows perseverance: continuing in spite of difficulty.

content.question: What is the main idea?
choices: B) Perseverance helped Rudolph overcome a hard start.

content.question: In the passage, “perseverance” means:
choices: D) Continuing in spite of difficulty

content.question: What can be inferred?
choices: C) Support from her family mattered.

content.question: Use perseverance in a sentence of your own.
